legacy_crosswalk.teacher_content: Heredity foundations, chromosome terminology, meiosis, crossing over, independent assortment, random fertilization
legacy_crosswalk.notes: Maps directly to current Meiosis and Meiosis and Genetic Diversity topics.

legacy_crosswalk.teacher_content: Mendel, alleles, dominance, segregation, independent assortment, Punnett squares, probability
legacy_crosswalk.notes: Maps to current Mendelian Genetics, including quantitative probability skills.

legacy_crosswalk.teacher_content: Incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, pedigrees, linked genes, recombination and gene mapping, sex-linked inheritance, organelle inheritance
legacy_crosswalk.notes: Maps primarily to Non-Mendelian Genetics. Pleiotropy is repaired from the current CED because it is not explicitly taught by name in the deck.

legacy_crosswalk.teacher_content: Observed versus expected values, chi-square calculation, degrees of freedom, p-value/table interpretation, null-hypothesis decisions
legacy_crosswalk.notes: Current Unit 5 requires chi-square hypothesis testing for inheritance data; source wording is preserved with corrected reject/fail-to-reject and p-value interpretation.
Maps to current Environmental Effects on Phenotype.
Supports chromosome segregation/nondisjunction and chromosomal inheritance concepts; named human examples remain contextual rather than universal phenotype rules.

items.evidence: Meiosis review plus explanation of crossing over, independent assortment, random fertilization, and synthesis of meiosis/fertilization as sources of variation.
Worked monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, gamete generation, genotype/phenotype probabilities, and 9:3:3:1 interpretation.
Multiplication and addition rules are applied to genetics probabilities and multilocus outcomes.
Pedigree symbols and qualitative inheritance-pattern clues are used to infer dominant and X-linked models.
Students distinguish incomplete dominance from codominance and solve cattle/ABO inheritance questions.
XX/XY X-linked crosses and disorder examples require tracking allele transmission by chromosome.
Parental/recombinant classification, linkage, crossing over, recombination frequency, map units, and the 50% limit are interpreted.
A complete chi-square goodness-of-fit workflow derives expected counts, calculates χ², obtains df, uses a critical-value table, and makes a hypothesis decision.
Environmental examples require explaining how one genotype can produce different phenotypes under different conditions.
Nondisjunction and trisomy-21 karyotype imagery connect segregation error with altered chromosome number.

next_required_output: F2 learning-function classification and palace architecture; do not write Unit 5 narrative prose before F2.
